messages.lesson.the.spring.was.released.too.early: The spring was released too early: attach it again, return to neutral and release below 0.3 kn.
messages.lesson.1.5.attach.the.spring.between.the: 1/5 · Attach the spring between the aft port cleat and the highlighted cleat towards the front of the finger pontoon.
messages.lesson.2.5.the.spring.is.attached.now.re: 2/5 · The spring is attached. Now release the original bow and stern lines.
messages.lesson.3.5.the.spring.is.slack.drag.it: 3/5 · The spring is slack: drag it down until it becomes taut.
messages.lesson.4.5.spring.taut.apply.gentle.aste: 4/5 · Spring taut: apply gentle astern, helm nearly centred, until the bow opens out by about 25°.
Bow sufficiently clear: return to neutral and wait for headway to fall before releasing.
messages.lesson.5.5.engine.in.neutral.release.the: 5/5 · Engine in neutral: release the spring, then gently engage ahead.
messages.lesson.spring.released.safely.move.ahead: Spring released safely: move ahead into the green zone without swinging the bow back towards the finger pontoon.
messages.lesson.1.6.align.with.the.berth.and.reve: 1/6 · Align with the berth and reverse slowly towards the centre berth.
messages.lesson.2.6.within.reach.of.the.quay.firs: 2/6 · Within reach of the quay, first attach the windward stern line to the indicated cleat.
messages.lesson.3.6.click.the.pickup.loop.at.the: 3/6 · Click the pickup loop at the quay, then a highlighted bow cleat.
messages.lesson.4.6.the.laid.mooring.is.being.car: 4/6 · The laid mooring is being carried forward: remain in neutral if it approaches the propeller.
5/6 · Laid mooring secured: now add the second stern line.
messages.lesson.6.6.adjust.all.three.lines.to.kee: 6/6 · Adjust all three lines to keep the stern 0.8 to 1.5 m from the quay, almost stationary.
messages.lesson.1.4.release.the.leeward.stern.lin: 1/4 · Release the leeward stern line first.
2/4 · Slacken and release the laid mooring, engine in neutral.
messages.lesson.3.4.keep.using.the.windward.stern: 3/4 · Keep using the windward stern line to control the bow, then release in neutral.
messages.lesson.4.4.all.lines.clear.leave.ahead.t: 4/4 · All lines clear: leave ahead towards the green zone.

messages.diagnostic.this.is.not.the.intended.spri: This is not the intended spring: connect the aft port cleat to the highlighted cleat towards the front.
The bow hit too hard. Restart and reduce headway earlier, before attaching the spring.
Crossed spring attached: drag its gauge down to take up slack and hold the bow.
messages.diagnostic.near.the.berth.connect.the.bo: Near the berth: connect the boat's forward port cleat to the end cleat on the finger pontoon, then gently take up the spring's slack.
Contact too fast: restart and reduce headway earlier. Wind helps turn the boat but does not slow it down.
messages.diagnostic.contact.is.too.fast.selecting: Contact is too fast. Selecting neutral earlier would give the fenders more time.
messages.diagnostic.gentle.contact.with.the.fende: Gentle contact with the fenders: they support the hull without a harsh rebound.
messages.diagnostic.pickup.selected.now.click.a.f: Pickup selected: now click a free bow cleat.
messages.diagnostic.first.cleat.chosen.click.a.co: First cleat chosen: click a compatible cleat on the other side to attach the line.
messages.diagnostic.astern.prop.walk.pushes.the.s: Astern, prop walk pushes the stern to port. The rudder only becomes useful with water flow.
messages.diagnostic.the.rudder.lacks.flow.without: The rudder lacks flow: without speed or propeller wash, it produces very little force.
messages.diagnostic.propeller.wash.hits.the.rudde: Propeller wash hits the rudder: the boat can turn before gaining much headway.
messages.diagnostic.throttle.is.neutral.but.inert: Throttle is neutral, but inertia preserves headway. Anticipate before reaching the pontoon.
messages.diagnostic.the.current.carries.the.whole: The current carries the whole boat. Watch speed over ground, which differs from speed through water.
messages.diagnostic.at.low.speed.wind.on.the.hull: At low speed, wind on the hull and mast can dominate rudder action.
messages.diagnostic.the.keel.resists.sideways.dri: The keel resists sideways drift. This resistance also shifts the boat's pivot point.
messages.diagnostic.apply.short.bursts.and.observ: Apply short bursts and observe the response before correcting again.

messages.scenario.dockForward.title: Leave the pontoon ahead
messages.scenario.dockForward.copy: The boat is moored stern to the pontoon between two fingers, with no wind or current. Move into the fairway before starting your turn.
messages.scenario.dockReverse.title: Leave the pontoon astern
messages.scenario.dockReverse.copy: The boat is moored bow to the pontoon between two fingers. Reverse into the fairway and observe how prop walk moves the stern.
messages.scenario.approach.title: Reach your berth
messages.scenario.approach.copy: You arrive from the outer basin with no wind or current. Follow the wide fairway, then enter the free berth alongside the south finger pontoon.
messages.scenario.approach.objective: Place the boat in the green outline alongside the finger pontoon, almost stopped and bow towards the pontoon.
messages.scenario.free.title: Outer basin
messages.scenario.free.copy: Start with short bursts. Observe how long the boat keeps moving when the throttle returns to neutral.
messages.scenario.inertia.title: Master inertia
messages.scenario.inertia.copy: Gain a little headway, then anticipate neutral and astern. Reach the target almost stopped.
messages.scenario.inertia.objective: Stop inside the circle, heading south, below 0.15 kn.
messages.scenario.halfTurn.title: Turn through 180° on the spot
messages.scenario.halfTurn.copy: The right-handed propeller moves the stern sideways astern: this is prop walk. Alternating short bursts ahead and astern lets you turn with little headway. Understand · Rotation shows the forces that turn the boat; hover over an arrow to read its details.
messages.scenario.halfTurn.objective: Turn the bow south while remaining in the starting circle, almost stopped.
messages.scenario.halfTurn.step.1: Set the helm hard to starboard and leave it there.
messages.scenario.halfTurn.step.2: Alternate full astern and full ahead quickly, without moving the helm. Watch the arrows at each reversal.
messages.scenario.dock.title: Berth bow first to port
messages.scenario.dock.copy: The crossed spring runs from the bow to the end of the finger pontoon, aft of the bow. It restrains movement towards the pontoon. Approach slowly: a line does not replace braking with the engine. You can pause the simulation to attach lines as if crew were helping.
messages.scenario.dock.objective: Place the boat in the green outline, almost stopped, crossed spring taut, with no impact above 0.20 m/s.
messages.scenario.dock.step.1: Move slowly towards the green outline, finger pontoon to port, then select neutral early enough to reduce headway.
messages.scenario.dock.step.2: Near the berth, click the forward port boat cleat, then the cleat at the end of the finger pontoon: the crossed spring is attached.
messages.scenario.dock.step.3: Take up slack using the line gauge to tension the spring, then stabilise the boat without letting the bow touch the pontoon.
messages.scenario.starboardDock.title: Berth to starboard with a north wind
messages.scenario.starboardDock.copy: Start heading north in the fairway, then turn to starboard towards the free berth by the breakwater. As the bow turns east, the north wind arrives on the port side and helps turn it towards the starboard finger pontoon. Use this assistance without letting the wind control your speed or contact point.
messages.scenario.starboardDock.objective: Enter the green outline, bow towards the breakwater, almost stopped, with no contact above 0.20 m/s.
messages.scenario.starboardDock.step.1: Move slowly north until level with the berth entrance; leave room to turn without crowding neighbouring boats.
messages.scenario.starboardDock.step.2: Set the helm to starboard with a short burst ahead. Watch the bow: wind helps it turn towards the finger pontoon but can increase sideways drift.
messages.scenario.starboardDock.step.3: Align parallel to the finger pontoon, select neutral early, then remove the remaining headway with a brief burst astern. Arrive starboard side alongside almost stopped, without hitting the breakwater.
messages.scenario.starboardDock.levelTwo.copy: Level 2 · The north wind now blows at 15 kn. It still helps the bow turn to starboard but pushes faster towards the finger pontoon: start the turn earlier and reduce headway before aligning.
messages.scenario.starboardDock.levelTwo.objectiv: With 15 kn of north wind, berth in the same outline, almost stopped, with no contact above 0.20 m/s.
messages.scenario.reverse.title: Depart astern
messages.scenario.reverse.copy: Reverse through the entrance. The right-handed propeller pushes the stern to port: compensate when the rudder gains flow.
messages.scenario.reverse.objective: Leave through the green rectangle astern without touching other boats.
messages.scenario.mooring.title: Leave on a spring
messages.scenario.mooring.copy: A crosswind holds you against the port finger pontoon. Rig an aft spring, use it as a pivot, then leave ahead.
messages.scenario.mooring.objective: Attach the indicated spring, take up slack, open the bow out by 20 to 35°, then release in neutral and reach the green zone.
messages.scenario.medDock.title: Berth with a laid mooring
messages.scenario.medDock.copy: Approach stern to the quay with 10 kn of crosswind. First hold the windward stern, pick up the laid mooring, then balance all three lines.
messages.scenario.medDock.objective: Reverse into the centre berth, secure the windward stern, carry the laid mooring to the bow, then finish with the second stern line.
messages.scenario.medDeparture.title: Depart from a laid mooring
messages.scenario.medDeparture.copy: The boat is stern to the quay, held by two stern lines and a bow laid mooring. Release lines in order and keep the propeller clear.
messages.scenario.medDeparture.objective: Release the leeward line, slacken and release the laid mooring in neutral, control the bow with the windward stern line, then leave ahead.
